title: European data guardrail: runtime adaptor for residency + tier-aware fallbacks
creator: Priya Narang
description: Implement a runtime adaptor that enforces EU-only data residency policies and supports tier-aware routing with deterministic fallback to model variants when EU capacity is constrained. This ticket covers the runtime enforcement layer, the per-customer residency allowlist/denylist integration, audit logging hooks, and the initial rollout plan. The goal is to prevent non-EU data egress for customers with residency requirements while preserving SLOs by gracefully degrading to approved fallbacks (region-equivalent variants or dedicated/private pools).
acceptance_criteria: Requests from customers marked 'eu_residency: strict' are only routed to EU-located model endpoints or private deployments pinned to EU regions
If no EU-hosted variant is available, runtime chooses a pre-authorized fallback model variant defined in customer config and increments fallback metrics
Allowlist/denylist changes propagate to the runtime within 30 seconds after control-plane update
All routed decisions emit the residency_decision audit event with request_id, customer_id, chosen_region, chosen_model_variant, and reason
E2E tests covering strict, permissive, and soft-enforcement modes pass in CI and on a canary cluster
tasks: Schema change: add customer_residency_policy to customer_config table (enum: none|soft|strict) and allowed_fallback_variants list
Runtime adaptor: implement ResidencyRouter component that queries local config cache and decides route according to policy priority (customer, org, global)
Implement fast allowlist/denylist cache with TTL and push invalidation from control plane
Fallback mapping: support per-customer ordered list of acceptable model variants and tiers (hosted->dedicated->private) with explicit cost/latency tags
Audit logging: add structured residency_decision event to tracing pipeline and to audit logs bucket
Feature flag gating and canary deployment manifest for 10% tenancy in eu-region cluster
Add unit + integration tests including simulated outages of eu-region to verify fallback behaviour
Update runtime docs and API error codes for RESIDENCY_VIOLATION and FALLBACK_USED
technical_notes: Decision ordering: customer residency policy overrides org-level; if policy == strict then deny any non-EU endpoint unless listed in allowed_fallback_variants
Enforcement layers: prefer enforcing at the edge router to save cost, but runtime must validate for private deployments since edge cannot see dedicated pool mapping
Cache strategy: use LRU local cache with changefeed from control plane to reduce control plane lookup latency; TTL default 30s with immediate invalidation on policy change

Fallback selection: pick first model variant that matches customer allowed list and has compatible architecture and quantization; if multiple variants available prefer lower-latency EU-hosted; include cost delta in telemetry
Circuit breaker: if fallback rate for a customer exceeds threshold (configurable), mark customer for extended audit and escalate to oncall
Compatibility: default customers with no residency policy behave as before (global routing) to avoid regressions
DB migration: backfill customer_residency_policy='none' for existing rows and empty allowed_fallback_variants; migration must be online and idempotent
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy schema + control-plane APIs behind feature flag; no runtime enforcement (read-only) - validate UI and CRUD flows
Stage 2: Enable runtime adaptor in canary (10% traffic) for non-critical customers; monitor fallback rate and misroutes metric
Stage 3: Expand canary to EU-region tenants with EU-residency=soft; run chaos test by disabling an EU pool to observe fallback behaviour
Stage 4: Gradual enablement for customers with EU-residency=strict after manual verification and signed policy acceptance
Stage 5: Full enforcement and deprecation of legacy permissive routing for new customers only
metrics: residency.resolved.total - total routing decisions evaluated for residency
residency.fallback.used - count of fallbacks triggered due to capacity or policy
residency.misroute.detected - detected non-compliant routes (should be zero for strict customers)
residency.policy.update.latency - time from control-plane set to runtime effective
